correctness.rationale: For every real 0<r<1, coercivity and strict convexity give a unique complex weighted L1 minimizer; symmetry reduces to real coefficients. A displayed tangent-half-angle derivative becomes odd under reciprocal scaling at c=2r/(1+r²), giving exact global stationarity. The minimum has an exact elliptic-integral algebraic decomposition. In the explicitly normalized degree-two Hardy model basis, the exact three weighted Fourier moments characterize the target rank-one compression. The displayed continuous unimodular-phase symbol has those moments by first-variation vanishing and oddness; Hölder duality proves the exact minimum and its almost-everywhere uniqueness. 70 high-precision numerical checks passed, supplementary to the analytical proof; no unjustified finite-to-continuum inference.

originality.rationale: The principal 2026 paper gives the identical quadratic test family but only a strict two-sided interval for the sharp symbol norm plus its boundary asymptotics. The present formula computes the unique complex weighted L1 optimizer, full finite-parameter elliptic norm, and unique exact L∞ symbol. The other close 2026 papers give weighted polynomial duality/general rank-one comparisons but no stated optimizing coefficient. Historical sources did not display the same result in accessible material. Unindexed older equivalent formulations remain a nontrivial risk; this is best-knowledge originality, not proof of uniqueness in the literature.
residual_risks: A classical weighted L1 best-approximation or Poisson-harmonic-measure formula in another notation may predate the motivating 2026 papers without being indexed by the searches.
The 2010 preprint arXiv:1009.5123 had only an abstract accessible in this check; no inference of full-document noncoverage is made.
The proof identifies a particular rank-one norm, not the supremum over all truncated Toeplitz operators on the same space; these quantities must not be conflated.
Full texts of historical general symbol papers beyond the 2009 accessible HTML may contain unindexed special-case calculations; none is knowingly claimed fully excluded.

value.rationale: The natural sharp finite-dimensional bounded-symbol problem is explicitly posed through a concrete rank-one family where only asymptotic rates and two-sided estimates were known. Solving the full Poisson-weighted two-mode approximation with an algebraic unique minimizer, elliptic value, and one explicit continuous optimal symbol supplies meaningful sharp constants and all equality cases. This is not a renaming of the known bounds; the involution identity provides an independent global-optimality mechanism with potential reuse. It does not claim universal results beyond quadratic model spaces.
